metadata.export_format: Session log JSON, abridged for IR
_notes: This file is abridged for incident-response analysis. The raw firewall log
contains 39 412 sessions involving 10.10.3.21 over the 14-day window.
The sessions reproduced below are: (1) all sessions to non-RFC1918
destinations, (2) all cross-VLAN sessions to the 10.10.20.0/24 server
segment, (3) all DNS sessions to non-internal resolvers, (4) representative
samples of benign internal traffic for baseline.
The full export is preserved in IR-FW-EXPORT-2026-05-16.json (1.8 GB).
Firewall timestamps are 4 seconds AHEAD of PCAP timestamps and Wazuh
timestamps because the firewall stamps the SYN at policy-decision time,
while host-side captures stamp at packet receipt. Use firewall ts as
authoritative for connection initiation per the 4x01 reconciliation note.

field_definitions.ts_start: Session start (firewall SYN timestamp), UTC ISO 8601
field_definitions.ts_end: Session end (FIN or last keepalive), UTC ISO 8601
field_definitions.classification: Analyst tag - BENIGN, BROWSING, INTERNAL, KNOWN_C2, SECONDARY_C2_HYPOTHESIS, EXFIL_BURST, LATERAL_MOVEMENT

sessions._section: ===== 2026-05-05: FIRST CREDENTIAL DUMP (host event, no obvious firewall change) =====

sessions._note: Beacon size INCREASED -- the typical beacon is 596/1042 bytes, this one is 1428/24814.  The 24 KB outbound is consistent with the dumped LSASS file out.dat being uploaded to the C2 (out.dat was 23 MB total; this 24 KB upload is the FIRST chunk -- additional chunks follow over the next 12 hours, see aggregate below).  This is the FIRST direct firewall evidence of credential theft exfil.

sessions._note_aggregate: [Between 2026-05-05T08:22 and 2026-05-05T20:00, KNOWN_C2 sessions show approximately 80 elevated-bytes sessions, summing to 23 884 219 bytes outbound -- consistent with the full LSASS dump (out.dat ~ 23 MB).  This is exfil of the credential-dump output.  Beacon cadence remains 5-minute but bytes_out per session climbed from 1 KB to 200 KB+ during this window.]

sessions._note: FIRST PsExec session WS-RECV-03 -> SRV-HEALTH-DB.  Cross-VLAN.  PsExec uses SMB on 445 to drop the service binary and pipe the IO.  This is the firewall evidence of the 4x04 H1 finding (which had no firewall visibility).  Anomaly: records03 has no business reason to access SRV-HEALTH-DB directly -- normal records03 access is through the EHR application via 8443, not direct SMB.
RPC mapper for WMI request (the wmiprvse spawn observed in 4x04 H2).
WMI dynamic-port channel (DCOM endpoint).  This is the WMIC dir / sc query enumeration (4x04 H2).

sessions._section: ===== 2026-05-07: SCHEDULED TASK CREATED + SECONDARY C2 FIRST CONNECTION =====

sessions._note: FIRST CONNECTION TO 203.0.113.47:8443.  This IP was NOT in any prior IOC.  It is on a Hetzner allocation (DE), not the LeaseWeb infrastructure used by 185.220.101.45.  No DNS query preceded this connection -- the IP was either hardcoded or delivered via the active 185.220.101.45 C2 in the prior 30 minutes.  The 8443 port is non-standard.  The connection profile (small upload, idle, then daily-ish reconnects) matches the 'secondary C2 channel on a non-standard port' description in HC3-2026-HEALTHBANE-004.

Continuation of the secondary C2 connection.  Bytes_in:bytes_out ratio is ~ 2:1 (downstream-heavy), consistent with a control channel receiving operator commands rather than a data exfil channel.  Connection went idle around 07:00:48 (last keepalive).
Scheduled task 02:00 CDT trigger (07:00 UTC).  This beacon is the kick-off for the day's exfiltrator run.

EXFIL BURST #1: 14.2 MB outbound to HEALTHBANE C2.  Size matches staging_export_001.zip exactly (14 219 484 bytes per disk_forensics_report.txt D1).  Transmitted at 02:38 CDT 2026-05-08, ~ 3 minutes after the staging archive was created (and immediately deleted on completion).  This is DIRECT NETWORK EVIDENCE of exfiltration of the 47 138-record patient table.

sessions._note_aggregate: [Day 2026-05-08 also saw normal records03 traffic during business hours: ~ 184 sessions to internet (browsing), ~ 41 sessions to SRV-FILE-01 (file work), ~ 18 sessions to SRV-MAIL-01 (Outlook).  All BENIGN; not reproduced individually.]

There is a 12-minute window where firewall sessions are CONTINUING to be logged (the firewall's logging is not affected by host-side wevtutil cl), but the host's Windows Security event log was cleared (per disk_forensics_report.txt Section 6, Security.evtx was deleted-and-recreated at 03:01:42 CDT = 08:01:42 UTC).  The discrepancy between firewall ts and host ts is the 4-second skew (firewall runs ~ 4s ahead).  Sessions continue to be reported below.
Notification beacon -- short upload after the log clear.  Possibly status / completion message back to C2.

EXFIL BURST #2: 11.8 MB outbound to HEALTHBANE C2.  Size matches staging_export_002.zip exactly (11 802 944 bytes per disk_forensics_report.txt D2).  Transmitted at 03:17 CDT 2026-05-11, ~ 2 minutes after archive creation.  This is DIRECT NETWORK EVIDENCE of exfiltration of the 51 002-record insurance policy table.

sessions._note: THIRD PsExec session WS-RECV-03 -> SRV-DC-01.  Domain Controller.  records03 cannot legitimately interact with the DC at the SMB layer.  Higher bytes_in than bytes_out is consistent with the AD enumeration (Get-ADUser) export from 4x04 H3.

sessions._section: ===== 2026-05-13 to 2026-05-14: ATTACKER QUIESCENT (only beacons + secondary C2 keepalives) =====

sessions._note: Scheduled task 02:00 CDT trigger.  Exfiltrator ran but received an EMPTY query response from the C2 config (the C2 config returned no useful query that day -- attacker may have been preparing to wind down).  No exfil burst followed.
13:42 CDT 2026-05-15:  WS-RECV-03 isolated by IR.  Outbound traffic to the C2 begins to be DENIED.  The RAT continues to attempt beacons at the 5-min interval, all blocked by the isolation rule.

sessions._note_aggregate: [Between 18:42:00Z and 19:42:00Z (the export cutoff), 12 additional beacon attempts to 185.220.101.45 are recorded, all DENY.  No further successful traffic from 10.10.3.21 to any external destination.]

summary._note: 168 sessions reproduced; the rest are aggregated by classification below.

SECONDARY_C2_HYPOTHESIS._note: FIRST seen on the day the scheduled task was registered.  Pattern is too low-volume to be a primary C2 -- consistent with a STANDBY / FALLBACK channel.  HC3-2026-HEALTHBANE-004 advisory describes this same pattern at peer victims.  CONFIDENCE: PROBABLE.

EXFIL_BURST._note: Three discrete bursts: 14.2 MB on 2026-05-08, 11.8 MB on 2026-05-11, 8.4 MB on 2026-05-13.  Bytes match disk-forensic deleted archives D1/D2/D3 to the byte.  These are the highest-confidence individual exfil events in the entire campaign.  Smaller cumulative LSASS-dump exfil over 2026-05-05 and 2026-05-12 is included in the KNOWN_C2 cumulative bytes_out above (~ 46 MB across the two cred-dump days).

LATERAL_MOVEMENT._note: Cross-VLAN.  records03 has NO BUSINESS REASON to access the 10.10.20.0/24 server segment from the 10.10.3.0/24 records-VLAN.  Existing firewall rule users-to-server-segment is overly permissive -- the IR recommendations should include tightening this rule to deny WS-* sources to SRV-* destinations except for explicit application ports.

key_findings_for_4x05_reconstruction: F1.  HEALTHBANE C2 to 185.220.101.45:443 is CONTINUOUS through the entire 14-day window (3958 beacons over 13.5 days = ~ 5-min interval).  Persistence is unbroken.

F2.  Secondary C2 to 203.0.113.47:8443 was FIRST established on 2026-05-07T06:48Z, which is the same day the scheduled task was registered (06:47:33Z).  The two events are 38 seconds apart -- the scheduled task creation is the trigger event for the secondary C2 setup.  This was a DELIBERATE redundancy operation by the attacker.
F3.  Exfiltration bytes are TIGHTLY CORRELATED with the disk-recovered staging archives.  The byte counts match exactly.  This is the strongest cross-evidence correlation in the entire investigation.

F4.  Cross-VLAN sessions to 10.10.20.0/24 from 10.10.3.21 (records03) are present on 6 distinct days (5/6, 5/9, 5/13 explicit; smaller follow-on sessions on other days).  Each cross-VLAN session sits exactly within the off-hours 02:00-04:00 CDT window.  None overlap with Robert Kim's WS-ADMIN-01 baseline.

F5.  HIPAA breach impact assessment based on firewall data: 47 138 + 51 002 = 98 140 patient + insurance records confirmed exfiltrated.  AD enumeration of 1184 records adds reconnaissance evidence but those are not patient records.  The 98 140-record figure is the basis for breach notification.
